title: Capacity to Deadline Optimizer
subtitle: Frontier Specialty Care Network (fictional) · 13,951 appointments and 1,786 waitlist entries · 6 months. Average lead time is 29.8 days and only 59.1% of appointments meet their specialty's access standard. Meanwhile 2,087 booked slots went unused through cancellation and no-show, and 507 of them were cancelled early enough to refill.
limitations: The fill simulation applies a flat refill rate to cancellations with enough notice; it assumes a matching patient is reachable and willing, which is the assumption most likely to break in practice. Waitlist match score weights are judgement, not fitted to acceptance outcomes. Lead time is calendar days from request to appointment and ignores patient-driven delay, so some of it is preference rather than access failure. The data is fully synthetic.
footer: Source: synthetic data generated by src/generate_data.py, seed 5150. No employer data, patient information, protected health information or confidential business information is used. Patient_Group is a synthetic cohort label, not a person.

queries.headline: SELECT COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(AVG(Lead_Time_Days),1) AS avg_lead, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Lead_Time_Within_Standard='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS within_std_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='No Show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Status IN ('Completed','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS no_show_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='Cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS cancel_pct, SUM(CASE WHEN Refillable='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refillable, SUM(CASE WHEN Status IN ('Cancelled','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unused_slots, ROUND(100.0*13951/14048,2) AS dq_score FROM appointments
queries.wl_head: SELECT COUNT(*) AS waiting, SUM(CASE WHEN Days_To_Requested_By<0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS past_requested, ROUND(AVG(Days_Waiting),1) AS avg_waiting, SUM(CASE WHEN Match_Priority IN ('High','Critical') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_priority FROM waitlist
queries.status: SELECT Status, COUNT(*) AS appointments FROM appointments GROUP BY Status ORDER BY appointments DESC
queries.by_specialty: SELECT a.Specialty, s.Target_Lead_Time_Days AS target_days, COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(AVG(a.Lead_Time_Days),1) AS avg_lead, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN a.Lead_Time_Within_Standard='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS within_std_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN a.Status='No Show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN a.Status IN ('Completed','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS no_show_pct FROM appointments a JOIN dim_specialty s ON s.Specialty=a.Specialty GROUP BY a.Specialty, s.Target_Lead_Time_Days ORDER BY within_std_pct
queries.reminder: SELECT CASE WHEN Reminder_Sent='Yes' THEN 'Reminder sent' ELSE 'No reminder' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='No Show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Status IN ('Completed','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS no_show_pct FROM appointments GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY no_show_pct
queries.lead_bands: SELECT CASE WHEN Lead_Time_Days<=14 THEN '0-14 days' WHEN Lead_Time_Days<=30 THEN '15-30 days' WHEN Lead_Time_Days<=60 THEN '31-60 days' ELSE '60+ days' END AS band, COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='No Show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Status IN ('Completed','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS no_show_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='Cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS cancel_pct FROM appointments GROUP BY band ORDER BY MIN(Lead_Time_Days)
queries.fill_sim: SELECT CAST(ROUND(Fill_Rate_Modeled) AS INT)||'% refill rate' AS scenario, Slots_Recovered AS slots, ROUND(Recovered_As_Pct_Of_Completed,2) AS pct_of_completed, Note FROM fill_simulation ORDER BY Fill_Rate_Modeled
queries.cancel_reasons: SELECT Cancellation_Reason, COUNT(*) AS cancellations, ROUND(AVG(Cancel_Notice_Days),1) AS avg_notice_days, SUM(CASE WHEN Refillable='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refillable FROM appointments WHERE Status='Cancelled' AND Cancellation_Reason IS NOT NULL AND Cancellation_Reason<>'' GROUP BY Cancellation_Reason ORDER BY cancellations DESC
queries.time_block: SELECT Time_Block, COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='No Show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Status IN ('Completed','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS no_show_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='Cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS cancel_pct FROM appointments GROUP BY Time_Block ORDER BY no_show_pct DESC
queries.by_hour: SELECT Appointment_Hour AS hour, COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Status='No Show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Status IN ('Completed','No Show') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS no_show_pct FROM appointments WHERE Appointment_Hour IS NOT NULL GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour
queries.capacity: SELECT Specialty, ROUND(SUM(Available_Slots),0) AS available, ROUND(SUM(Booked_Slots),0) AS booked, ROUND(SUM(Cancelled_Slots+No_Show_Slots),0) AS lost, ROUND(100.0*SUM(Booked_Slots)/NULLIF(SUM(Available_Slots),0),1) AS utilisation_pct FROM provider_capacity GROUP BY Specialty ORDER BY utilisation_pct DESC
queries.wl_priority: SELECT Match_Priority, COUNT(*) AS entries, ROUND(AVG(Days_Waiting),1) AS avg_waiting, ROUND(AVG(Waitlist_Match_Score),1) AS avg_score, SUM(CASE WHEN Days_To_Requested_By<0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS past_requested FROM waitlist GROUP BY Match_Priority ORDER BY avg_score DESC
queries.wl_specialty: SELECT Specialty, COUNT(*) AS entries, ROUND(AVG(Days_Waiting),1) AS avg_waiting, ROUND(AVG(Slots_Per_Waiting_Patient),3) AS slots_per_patient, SUM(CASE WHEN Days_To_Requested_By<0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS past_requested FROM waitlist GROUP BY Specialty ORDER BY slots_per_patient
queries.optin: SELECT CASE WHEN Notification_Opt_In='Yes' THEN 'Opted in to notifications' ELSE 'Not opted in' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS entries, SUM(CASE WHEN Offered_Slot_Date IS NOT NULL AND Offered_Slot_Date<>'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS offers_made, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Offer_Accepted='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Offered_Slot_Date IS NOT NULL AND Offered_Slot_Date<>'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS acceptance_pct FROM waitlist GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY acceptance_pct DESC
queries.monthly: SELECT substr(Request_Date,1,7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS appointments, ROUND(AVG(Lead_Time_Days),1) AS avg_lead, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Lead_Time_Within_Standard='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS within_std_pct FROM appointments WHERE Request_Date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
queries.wl_queue: SELECT Waitlist_ID, Specialty, Days_Waiting, Days_To_Requested_By, Preferred_Time, Travel_Category, Notification_Opt_In, ROUND(Waitlist_Match_Score,1) AS score, Match_Priority FROM waitlist ORDER BY Waitlist_Match_Score DESC, Days_Waiting DESC LIMIT 25
queries.exceptions: SELECT Rule_ID, Severity, Action_Taken, COUNT(*) AS exceptions FROM dq_exceptions GROUP BY Rule_ID, Severity, Action_Taken ORDER BY exceptions DESC

cards.title: Lead time against each specialty's own access standard
cards.desc: Bars are average lead time, the grey bar is the target that specialty is held to. Two specialties are inside their target and still generate complaints, because the average hides the tail.

cards.title: Appointment outcomes
cards.desc: Every booked slot in the period. The Cancelled and No Show wedges are the capacity the fill model is trying to recover.

cards.title: Compliance with access standard, by specialty
cards.desc: Worst first, against the blended 59.14% reported to the board.

cards.title: The reminder effect
cards.desc: The largest single effect on this page: no-shows are roughly three times higher without a reminder. Reminders are not randomly assigned here, so this is an association in the generated data, not a measured treatment effect.

cards.title: Longer waits, worse attendance
cards.desc: No-show rate more than doubles from the shortest to the longest lead-time band. Access delay and attendance are the same problem, which means fixing lead time pays twice.

cards.title: What refilling cancelled slots would actually buy
cards.desc: Three modelled refill rates against the 507 cancellations with enough notice. Even the optimistic scenario recovers under 4% of completed volume — worth doing, and not the answer to a 29.8-day lead time. Reporting the ceiling honestly is the point of the exercise.

cards.title: Cancellation reasons and how much notice they give
cards.desc: Notice days decide whether a cancellation is recoverable. The reasons giving most notice are the ones a waitlist offer can realistically fill.

cards.title: No-shows by time of day
cards.desc: Hour of the scheduled appointment. Useful for deciding where to put the slots most likely to be wasted, and for deciding which blocks to over-book.

cards.title: Time block performance
cards.desc: The same effect aggregated into the blocks schedulers actually work with.

cards.title: Capacity utilisation by specialty
cards.desc: Booked against available slots, with the slots lost to cancellation and no-show alongside. A specialty near full utilisation cannot absorb waitlist demand no matter how well the waitlist is scored.

cards.title: Waitlist by match priority
cards.desc: The score sorts the waitlist into four bands. Critical holds 316 entries — a real call list a scheduling team could work through, which is the test of whether a prioritisation model is usable rather than decorative. Average days waiting rises with the score, as it should.

cards.title: Where the waitlist pressure is
cards.desc: Slots per waiting patient is the supply-demand ratio that decides whether waiting is a scheduling problem or a capacity problem. The specialties at the top of this table cannot be scheduled out of their backlog.

cards.title: Notification opt-in — a null finding, reported anyway
cards.desc: The obvious hypothesis was that patients who opted in to notifications accept an offered slot more often. They do not: 54.0% against 55.87%, measured over the 563 offers actually made, which is the only denominator that answers the question — counting patients who were never offered a slot buries the effect. A gap that small on that base is noise. The match score still weights opt-in, because reachability matters operationally even where acceptance does not differ, and that weight is unvalidated. Reported here rather than dropped.

cards.title: Monthly trend
cards.desc: Grouped by request month, which is the six-month study window; grouping by appointment date instead produces a collapsing line that is a censoring artefact, not a trend. On this basis nothing moves: lead time holds at 29–30 days and compliance at 58–61% for six straight months. Bars are appointment volume on the right axis.

cards.title: Waitlist call list — highest match score first
cards.desc: Ranked by match score then days waiting. Days to requested-by is negative where the date has already passed. Preferred time and travel category are included because a scheduler needs them to make the call, not to admire the model.

cards.title: Data quality exception log
cards.desc: 376 exceptions across appointments and waitlist, with what was done about each. 63 records were excluded from reporting and logged rather than repaired.
